mainEntity.name: How much does a Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D (4M41) engine replacement typically costs between £1,500 and £4,800 for the engine supply alone, depending on whether you choose used, reconditioned, or rebuilt. Supply and fit adds approximately £1,000-£1,600 in specialist 4x4 labour. Dealer pricing can add 30-50% to these figures.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D (4M41) has a timing chain, not a belt. This is a metal chain that should last the engine's lifetime under proper maintenance, but timing chain tensioner wear is a known issue. If you hear rattling on cold start, have the chain and tensioner inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the Shogun 4M41 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 4M41 has three well-documented weak points: timing chain tensioner wear causing cold-start rattle, turbocharger actuator failure causing loss of power, and injector/pump failure causing hard starting. Off-road usage patterns accelerate these failures compared to standard applications.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on the vehicle's value and condition. A typical Shogun 3.2 DI-D is worth £4,000-£14,000. A rebuilt engine at £2,800-£4,800 may represent a significant portion of the vehicle's value. If the 4x4 is in good condition, well-maintained, and you intend to keep it for 2+ years, replacement is often worthwhile. If vehicle value is under £4,000, evaluate scrap value first.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between 4M41 and 4M40 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 4M41 is the later 3.2-litre DI-D turbo diesel (1999-2021) with common-rail fuel injection and timing chain design, available in 160-200hp outputs. The 4M40 is the earlier 2.8-litre turbo diesel (1991-2000) with 125-140hp, mechanical injection, and timing belt design. The 4M41 is the more common and more powerful engine in UK Shoguns.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D engine replacement typically takes 2-4 working days. Specialist 4x4 workshops can complete the job in 14-18 labour hours. Supply lead times vary: used engines 2-5 working days, reconditioned 5-10 working days, and rebuilt 7-14 working days. Confirm exact timelines with your chosen specialist.

historyTimeline.h2: Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D (4M41) was introduced in 1999 as the flagship diesel engine for the Shogun/Pajero range. This 3.2-litre common-rail turbo diesel with intercooler became the definitive Shogun engine across two generations .

milestones.description: 4M41 introduced, 3.2-litre DI-D turbo diesel, 160hp - launched with Shogun/Pajero III (V6_W/V7_W chassis)
2006 - Early 4M41 with 118kW (160hp) output; timing chain engine design
2007 - 4M41 fitted to Shogun II and III across SWB/LWB variants
Fourth-generation Shogun/Pajero IV (V8_W/V9_W chassis) introduced; 4M41 upgraded
Significant power upgrade: 147kW (200hp) and 441Nm torque - 18% increase over outgoing diesel
2019 - 4M41 continues across NS, NT, NW, NX model codes with 160-200hp outputs
End of Shogun production; 4M41 remains available through specialist suppliers

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D (4M41) is a robust engine but has three well-documented weak points that can lead to costly repairs. Timing chain tensioner wear, turbocharger actuator failure, and injector/pump problems are the primary failure drivers. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: High carbon deposits in the engine oil accelerate timing chain tensioner wear; the tensioner can stick and fail to tension the chain, causing a rattling noise on cold start . The 4M41 uses a timing chain design with no fixed replacement interval, making regular inspection critical .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and inspect tensioner for wear and plunger extension
Replace chain, tensioner, guides, and sprockets
Supply & fit rebuilt 4M41 with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has broken causing internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Mitsubishi Shogun 3.2 DI-D of relevant age is worth approximately £4,000-£14,000 depending on mileage and condition. The replacement-to-value guidance is: - Vehicle worth under ~£4,000: scrap threshold - replacement may exceed vehicle value - Vehicle worth ~£4,000-£8,000: evaluate both; used engine may be better value - Vehicle worth ~£8,000+: replacement usually cost-effective
problems.recommendation: Do not ignore timing chain rattling on a cold start - it's a progressive issue and the noise is a warning . A specialist can diagnose whether the tensioner alone needs replacing or if the full kit is required. Replacement costs are significantly lower if caught early.
